<description>
This implements the Consensus Cleanup validation rules proposed in [BIP 54](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0054.md). These rules are only enabled on regtest. Mainnet activation, if any, is to be considered separately.

This patchset is based on the code that was previously reviewed ([1](https://github.com/bitcoin-inquisition/bitcoin/pull/99), [2](https://github.com/bitcoin-inquisition/bitcoin/pull/110)) and tested (for instance [here](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/consensus-cleanup-demo-of-slow-blocks-on-signet/2367)) on Bitcoin Inquisition. The tests and documentation have since been improved, but the consensus-critical commits have been carried over with only minor differences (the only behavioural one being the addition of the stripped-size check to `PreChecks`).

Roughly 95% of the added lines are tests or test data. The format, contents, and reproduction procedure for the BIP 54 test vectors are documented [here](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/tree/master/bip-0054/test_vectors). The `bip54_tests` unit test module exercises each mitigation extensively in isolation. The `feature_bip54.py` functional test verifies all of them end-to-end after and prior to activation. For the timestamp rules, it simulates timewarp and Murch–Zawy attacks, demonstrating the new timestamp rules prevent these exploits. A fuzz harness for the sigop accounting logic is also included, which can be seeded from the BIP test vectors (implemented [here](https://github.com/darosior/bitcoin/tree/bip54_seed_fuzz_corpus)).

See commit messages for details.
</description>

[quoted text omitted]

This commit breaks existing `getblocktemplate` calls on Regtest. With `gbt_optional_rule = false` and `ALWAYS_ACTIVE` on Regtest, a `getblocktemplate` call now has to include `"consensuscleanup"` in the `"rules"` (`{"rules": ["segwit", "consensuscleanup"]}`). Otherwise the error `"Support for 'consensuscleanup' rule requires explicit client support"` is returned. This affects external mining software, Stratum proxies, and other projects' integration tests. In our tests this works as `NORMAL_GBT_REQUEST_PARAMS` is updated too.
This is a behavior change that warrants mentioning in release notes. Making the rule optional (`gbt_optional_rule = true`) is another option for discussion.

[2026-10-27] rc:4387813407 inline on src/validation.cpp by optout21 (contributor) (edited 2026-10-27):
[quoted text omitted]

Unconditional consensus error at mempool check. 64-byte transactions are rejected from mempool with consensus error now, regardless of deployment (so on mainnet as well). This is inconsistent, as such transactions are considered consensus-valid at block checking. The status quo is rejecting 64-byte transactions with non-standardness error. Therefore the behavior is unchanged, only the error is changed from non-standard to invalid in this case.

All this seems intended behavior. Nonetheless, I think it would make sense to explicitly mention this inconsistency in:

- a code comment here
- in the commit message
- in the PR description
- in release notes (?)

The discarded alternative is to reject with consensus failure only if BIP54 is active, otherwise leave the non-standardness rejection.

The 64-byte rule is tested on BIP54-active chain (RegTest) only, not on non-active chain. I recommend adding a test on mainnet, to verify non-activation on mainnet (at current heights).
[2026-10-27] rc:4387846132 inline on src/validation.cpp by optout21 (contributor) (edited 2026-10-27):
[quoted text omitted]

Minor optimization observation: a custom, `IsSizeInvalid()` method could perform faster than the generic compute-size-and-compare-to-64. However, the difference is minimal, especially compared to costly part of block validation.
Nonetheless, a custom method would make the intent more explicit and leave room for further optimization.

Sample `IsSizeInvalid()` implementation

```C++
/** Whether the witness-stripped serialized size of this transaction is exactly 64 bytes (BIP 54). */
bool IsSizeInvalid(const CTransaction& tx)
{
    // Each input takes at least 41 and each output at least 9 non-witness bytes, on top of
    // 10 bytes for the version, locktime and the input and output counts.
    if (10 + 41 * tx.vin.size() + 9 * tx.vout.size() > INVALID_TX_NONWITNESS_SIZE) return false;
    return ::GetSerializeSize(TX_NO_WITNESS(tx)) == INVALID_TX_NONWITNESS_SIZE;
}
```
